hard_prerequisites.requirement: Yak-52 R6 must pass reference-locked Blender production, Unreal import, close-view visual review, cockpit geometry, canopy state, sockets and collision acceptance.
The current Mission 1 environment source must compile, the Recovery05 proof must pass, and the representative production environment proof must be accepted before final combat integration.

parallel_safe_offline_work: naming, socket, material-slot and animation-state contracts
strict source-only verifier and test design
gate_dependencies.heavy_gate_rule: Every Blender production, Unreal import, native build, integration, capture, profiling or packaging attempt requires its own explicit one-shot authorization.

rules: Every candidate uses a fresh immutable attempt namespace.
Failed attempts are never overwritten, renamed, reused or automatically retried.
Accepted source, exports, imports, renders, logs, receipts and manifests are hash-frozen together.
No candidate becomes runtime authority through naming, presence or a successful tool exit alone.

disallowed_as_production_authority.policy: These assets may remain immutable historical or engineering evidence, but they cannot satisfy any production-art acceptance criterion and cannot be the selected mesh in a final candidate.

reference_and_scale: A dimensioned, source-cited reference board is frozen before modeling.
Scale, orientation, origin, pivots, material slots and socket coordinates are recorded in centimeters and verified after Unreal import.
Reference uncertainty is disclosed; no unsupported detail is promoted as factual.
geometry_and_uv: Close-view silhouette is continuous, correctly proportioned and free of disconnected slabs, floating members or primitive fallback forms.
Subdivision/high-poly or equivalent source supports believable bevels, panel transitions and manufactured forms.
Production retopology, Nanite strategy or skeletal topology is chosen per asset and justified by measured screen use.
UVs have no unintended overlap, required padding at final mip resolution, consistent texel density and dedicated lightmap handling where applicable.
Collision is authored for gameplay purpose and independently checked against visible geometry.
materials_and_textures: Calibrated PBR base color, normal and packed roughness/metallic/AO data are supplied; emissive, opacity, thickness or masks are added only where physically justified.
No baked directional lighting, crushed AO, normal-map projection contamination or featureless overexposure is accepted.
Macro variation, micro detail, decals and controlled wear remain material-appropriate under daylight, overcast, night, wet and storm lighting.
Every third-party texture or material used in a final candidate has a passing final-use provenance receipt.
visual_review: Original-resolution images are inspected directly, not only thumbnails or automated statistics.
Each close-view asset has fixed daylight, overcast, night/wet, grazing-angle and gameplay-context cameras.
First-person assets include hip, ADS, recoil, reload, left-look, right-look, canopy-edge and pilot-protection views.
Temporal review rejects mesh jitter, camera-coupled world motion, LOD popping, unstable materials, clipping or animation discontinuity.
A successful import, render or automation exit never substitutes for human visual acceptance.
runtime_and_packaging: No synchronous asset load, runtime mesh construction, shader compilation or unbounded allocation occurs inside firing, impact, damage or destruction paths.
Required assets, Niagara systems, audio voices and breakup actors are pooled or prewarmed before play.
Final validation runs from a fresh packaged Development candidate and is repeated for the Shipping candidate.
Asset Registry, cook and packaged dependency scans prove no disallowed proxy or retired WebGame asset is selected by the accepted runtime path.

lanes.name: Pilot and rear-gunner production characters
depends_on: accepted Yak-52 R6 cockpit, seats, canopy, camera, protection volumes and sockets
deliverables: production pilot and rear-gunner meshes
shared or governed skeleton and physics assets
seat, harness, head, eye, shoulder, hand and weapon sockets
seated idle, look, brace, fire, reload, Igla raise/lower and reaction poses
acceptance: anatomy, scale and seated posture are believable from rear-gunner and exterior cameras
pilot, gunner, harness and airframe never interpenetrate through the governed motion range
pilot remains protected from rifle and missile firing traces in every weapon state
rear canopy remains visibly open for the gunner while the pilot canopy reads as closed and protective

lanes.name: Arms, sleeves and gloves
depends_on: G7.1 skeleton, shoulder, elbow, wrist and weapon socket contract
deliverables: anatomical upper arms, forearms, hands and articulated fingers
leather glove materials with seams, folds, roughness and wear
two-hand rifle grips, Igla grips, recoil support and reload poses
first-person corrective shapes and IK targets
acceptance: no block, cylinder or sphere primitive reads as a human limb
finger contact, wrist angle and forearm volume remain credible through hip, ADS, fire and reload states
no clipping through the rifle, Igla, canopy, cockpit rim or pilot
skin, sleeve and glove materials remain distinct under all required lighting

lanes.name: Production rifle and physical ADS
depends_on: G7.1 and G7.2 sockets, poses and safe firing arcs
deliverables: production rifle with high/low or Nanite source, calibrated PBR materials and physical iron sights
muzzle, eject, left-hand, right-hand and ADS sockets
hip-to-ADS, recoil, recovery, reload and manipulation animations
muzzle flash, casing, impact and spatial audio integration
acceptance: right mouse holds ADS and left mouse fires while ADS remains held
front post and rear aperture align physically with the camera without a HUD reticle or crosshair
weapon does not fire through the pilot, protected cockpit, canopy or airframe
muzzle effects originate from the barrel and do not obscure the sight picture
model, hands and sights remain stable during aircraft motion, banking and recoil

lanes.name: Production Igla and missile
depends_on: G7.1 and G7.2 sockets, poses and safe firing arcs
deliverables: production launcher, sighting/control hardware and separate missile
launcher rear, forward muzzle, seeker, exhaust and hand sockets
raise, acquire, track, fire, recoil/backblast presentation, lower and reload states
lock acquire, decay, loss and launch feedback using audio and diegetic presentation
acceptance: missile visibly exits the forward end with correct orientation
lock eligibility respects target class, line of sight, seeker cone and acquire/decay timing
launch is blocked by the pilot, canopy, airframe and unsafe arcs
missile trail, exhaust, detonation and audio are spatial, pooled and free of first-use stalls

lanes.name: Shahed and heavy-drone production families
deliverables: standard and heavy production silhouettes
propulsion, control-surface and material variants
intact, damaged, critical, breakup and wreck states
governed collision, hit zones, LOD/Nanite strategy and destruction sockets
acceptance: each variant is recognizable at engagement distance and credible at close flyby distance
damage progression is readable without relying on a HUD reticle
breakup follows authored pieces and pooled effects rather than spawning unbounded primitives
destroyed drones produce impact/explosion audio, not placeholder pew sounds
no drone breakup or cleanup path causes a visible multi-second freeze

realistic spatial rifle, Igla, impact, explosion, debris, engine, wind, ocean, city and radio audio
voice, debris and effect concurrency budgets
prewarm manifest and first-use shader/PSO evidence

lanes.name: Mission 1 combat integration and packaged proof
depends_on: accepted Mission 1 environment and Yak-52 R6
deliverables: fresh packaged Development candidate
three accepted 1920x1080 input-driven combat captures
one accepted 20-minute input-driven combat soak
ADS rifle, Igla, drone breakup, boss destruction and weather-fast-camera traces
contextual shader/PSO review and machine-readable terminal receipts
acceptance: all 15 existing performance bookmark literals are exercised in context
no ADS/fire freeze, drone-breakup stall, boss-destruction stall, crash, timeout or material restoration failure
frozen frame-time, hitch, GPU, memory, VRAM and stability rubrics pass
pilot/airframe firing protection passes for rifle and Igla in every camera and weapon state
original-resolution gameplay captures pass direct visual inspection
the Shipping candidate repeats the accepted input, combat, save/settings and stability gates before release

required_lane_evidence: dimensioned reference board and source provenance
object, material, UV, skeleton, socket, pivot and collision inventory
tool stdout, stderr, PID, actual numeric exit code and timeout status
Unreal import, Asset Registry, cook and dependency receipts
performance, stability and packaged-game evidence appropriate to the lane

prohibitions: No lane is accepted because a file exists, a tool exits zero, or an automated count passes.
No failed attempt is repaired in place or silently replaced.
No production candidate is integrated before all upstream hashes and visual decisions are frozen.
No Gate 7 completion claim is allowed while any proxy, WebGame, L88 or engine primitive remains selected by the accepted runtime path.
